labeler: single labeler (the benchmark author) from the maintainers' fix or the construction design; a second blind mapper is registered in the protocol and must run before freeze

pw-n01.rationale: Action on a server-rendered page right after goto had no effect and surfaced only at the next wait; hydration replaced the control. Matches the F15 definition.

pw-n02.rationale: Click on a server-rendered trigger before the client handler attached, no error, menu never opens, passes on retry: the F15 signature.

pw-n03.rationale: The action's postcondition was not awaited before dependent work: action completed but the wrong (stale) state remained.

pw-n04.rationale: A step ran before the previous action's end state was reached (payment completed): missing postcondition wait.

pw-n05.rationale: Test assumes an order of completion among parallel async responses; the first-finished slot decides the outcome.

pw-n06.rationale: Content not yet rendered when a single-shot read ran. F14's wording ('content not yet rendered ... a window the assertion can miss') fits; F1 is the generic alternative, hence forced.

pw-n07.rationale: A transient element lingers during a ~200 ms close animation and makes a locator ambiguous; root cause is the animation window, the strict-mode error is the symptom.

pw-n08.rationale: A transient element (the closing form) still present when the assertion reads; classic window the assertion can miss.

pw-n09.rationale: Passes locally, fails only on slower CI runner hardware because the input speed is environment dependent.

pw-n10.rationale: Locator matched two elements (strict mode violation) because it was never specific enough; the DOM did not change.

pw-n11.rationale: Textbook strict mode violation from an over-broad name regex; no DOM change is reported.

pw-n12.rationale: Strict mode violation from a non-exact name; the timing only decides when the second match appears.

pw-n13.rationale: Strict mode violation (F2) whose trigger is a branch-specific DOM difference (F12-like); F2 chosen because the locator itself was ambiguous.

pw-n14.rationale: Page content changed (a second demo was added) and the test's locator was not updated; the change that broke it is named.

pw-n15.rationale: A feature PR changed the DOM and the page object's locators were not updated.

pw-n16.rationale: Product DOM changed after the test was written (new role=alert); the test locator was not updated.

pw-n17.rationale: Page object locators too broad for content that sub-pages now add; F12 (POM) vs F2 (strict violation) is a close call.

pw-n18.rationale: Failure is a dropped network connection during a proxied request (F3), caused by test-side interception volume under load; F8 (CI-only) is the alternative.

pw-s01.rationale: Plain duration-near-timeout, passes on retry, no state or selector evidence.

pw-s02.rationale: Deterministic expected-vs-received mismatch with no timing, selector, or data issue; the expectation is wrong.

pw-s03.rationale: Assertion mismatch whose expectation is right and the product result is wrong (product regression); F9 (catalogue data) is the alternative.

pw-s04.rationale: The action's outcome (save) was not awaited before the dependent step; the wrong state remains after the action.

pw-s05.rationale: An element that is conditionally present is acted on as if it always exists.

pw-s06.rationale: Conditional UI per account type; step and assertion always run.

pw-s07.rationale: Passes alone, fails in the suite, leaked localStorage state.

pw-s09.rationale: Hard-coded id that only exists in some data sets.

pw-s10.rationale: Expired session reused from a saved state; redirected to login.

pw-s11.rationale: Role-based UI not rendered for the session in use.

pw-s12.rationale: Assumes an order of completion between two parallel requests.

pw-s13.rationale: A failure is swallowed by .catch(() => {}); a later test fails with a misleading symptom.

pw-s14.rationale: The failing assertion is caught and logged; the test passes while the behaviour is broken.

pw-s15.rationale: SSR page; first interaction after goto had no effect; passes on retry.

pw-s16.rationale: Server-rendered control acted on after goto, appears to succeed but has no effect; surfaces at the next assertion; passes on retry.

cy-n01.rationale: State/requests leak from one test to the next through a shared route; the failing assertion depends on what the previous test left behind.

cy-n02.rationale: Tests share page and dialog state; the second test inherits what the first left open.

cy-n03.rationale: A transient state (errors flash for ~50 ms) that a single non-retrying read can hit.

cy-n04.rationale: Content re-renders during a window the test captured an element in; F14 (transient/not-yet-rendered content) vs F1 (generic timing) is a close call.

cy-n05.rationale: The menu (element) disappears within a few ms after it appears, in a window the test cannot control; product-side cause, so F14 is the closest code.

cy-n06.rationale: The failure comes from running requests under a logged-out session and waiting on the login call's alias; auth/session ordering is the cause, with some stale-alias flavor.

cy-n07.rationale: The test's data (mock listing) no longer matches what the product requires; two causes in one fix, the crash comes from missing data, hence forced.

cy-n08.rationale: Deterministic failure on one environment configuration (custom context path) that passes in the default one.

cy-n09.rationale: An external network dependency (docs.appsmith.com unreachable/slow) makes the test hang; no product or test logic cause.

cy-n10.rationale: Unmocked API call returned 401 (F3: unexpected API response); the redirect to /login is the downstream session effect (F10).

cy-s01.rationale: Duration equals the timeout and the retry passes; slow legitimate operation.

cy-s02.rationale: Fixed sleep versus variable latency: the classic flaky timing case; F5 and F14 are plausible alternates.

cy-s04.rationale: Expected-vs-received mismatch on a text label (F4); the label rename could also be called drift (F12).

cy-s05.rationale: Action completed, but the assertion reads the old state before the follow-up update; missing wait for the result.

cy-s06.rationale: Conditional UI handled as unconditional (F6); state carried from another spec (F7) is the alternate.

cy-s07.rationale: Conditionally present element assumed present (F6); the data of the tenant (F9) decides when.

cy-s08.rationale: Leaked preference state across specs; passes alone.

cy-s09.rationale: Time-of-day / time zone dependent result differing between environments.

cy-s10.rationale: Missing seed data / hard-coded user record; the 401 is a consequence.

cy-s11.rationale: Session expired mid-suite; redirect to sign-in.

cy-s12.rationale: Out-of-order completion of parallel async requests determines the result.

cy-s13.rationale: Assumes completion order of two parallel requests (F11) but could be read as a missing wait (F5).

cy-s14.rationale: Errors are swallowed in the helper; the test passes while the behaviour is broken.

cy-s15.rationale: The initial failure (404) is silenced by failOnStatusCode:false and surfaces as an unrelated assertion; F3 is the alternate.

cy-s16.rationale: SSR framework, first interaction after visit has no effect, passes on retry.

pw-n19.rationale: The locator was too broad from the start (it also matched footnotes); the DOM did not change. The wrong element is picked only while the feed is still missing.

pw-n20.rationale: Playwright strict mode violation on a substring text locator that matches four elements; the page content did not change.

pw-n21.rationale: Unscoped getByRole('button') is ambiguous as soon as a second button exists; the failure only looks intermittent because the extra button appears at a variable time.

pw-n22.rationale: Locator ambiguity (two matches) is reported as a strict mode violation that does not retry; the second copy exists only during streaming.

pw-n23.rationale: A page change (a new heading) made an existing substring locator ambiguous; the product change is named and the test locator was not updated.

pw-n24.rationale: A DOM addition elsewhere on the page broke a previously unambiguous locator, and the cause pull request is named.

pw-n25.rationale: A merged UI change added a second element with the same accessible name; the test locator was not updated and the cause is named.

pw-n26.rationale: Page copy changed and the test still looks for the old text; the DOM drift is the only cause.

pw-n27.rationale: The UI label changed and the test locator was not updated; the element exists under a new accessible name.

pw-n28.rationale: A shared page-object locator was updated for the new DOM and no longer matches the older clients' DOM; the change is named.

pw-n29.rationale: The element exists under a different accessible name than the page object expects, which is locator drift; no specific product change is named, so the fit is only partial.

pw-n30.rationale: Product screen redesigned; every locator in the spec points at removed elements. The product change is named.

pw-n31.rationale: A fixed wall-clock sleep that is sometimes too short on a slow runner: timing flake that passes on a fast run and fails near the sleep budget.

pw-n32.rationale: Fixed 100 ms wait followed by a read that races a later frame; the read is too early on a slow run and passes on a fast one.

pw-n33.rationale: Failures are timeouts near the budget that pass on a warm server; the load-dependent slow start is the timing cause.

cy-n11.rationale: The test acts before an asynchronous fetch it depends on has completed; guessing the timing with an extra click is the race.

pw-n34.rationale: The failure is a timeout on a read that only succeeds when the runner is fast enough; the fix is defensive, so the mechanism is only loosely a timing one.

pw-n35.rationale: The assertion reads a state that exists only before rendering settles: content not yet painted. The window is a render, not a duration, so the fit is imperfect.

pw-n36.rationale: First interaction on a server-rendered page before the client handlers are attached: the click reports success but has no effect and the failure appears at the next assertion.

cy-n12.rationale: The step assumes the previous add has finished re-rendering before the next input is used; the condition, not a sleep, is what is missing.

pw-n37.rationale: The step assumes an asynchronous load has finished; the order of image load and test action decides the outcome.

cy-n13.rationale: Two asynchronous loads and an intercept registered after the navigation: the order in which responses and test steps happen is not controlled.

cy-n14.rationale: Two server responses (the poll and the sort click) can arrive in either order; the test assumes the sort response is the one it intercepted.

pw-n38.rationale: An asynchronous prefill and the test's fill race, and the replay order depends on which finishes first.

pw-n39.rationale: Keyboard input assumes the re-render scheduled by the helper has completed; the race is between an asynchronous render and the test, not a pure duration.

pw-n40.rationale: A one-time read assumes the page has finished adding elements; whether the second element exists yet depends on script timing.

pw-n41.rationale: The navigation step is reported as complete (URL changed) while the page state the next action needs is not there yet; the missing wait is for the new content.

pw-n42.rationale: The wait signal was already true, so the action proceeded while the state it needs was absent; the missing condition is the data itself.

pw-n43.rationale: State left by an earlier step (a toast) leaks into the next step; it is the same test, so the fit to the suite-level isolation definition is loose.

pw-n44.rationale: An element is present twice only during an animation window, which the click can hit or miss; the fix waits for the transient element to go away.

cy-n15.rationale: The element the test holds is replaced within a short window by a re-render; the test acts on a node that no longer exists.

cy-n16.rationale: The target element is replaced by Angular re-renders in the window between locating it and clicking it.

cy-n17.rationale: A net::ERR_ failure on the request to an external service endpoint in the test environment, with the test and the application unchanged.

pw-n45.rationale: The failure is a connection error from a network endpoint (here a local fixture server), reported as EPIPE or ECONNRESET, and it appears only under load.

pw-n46.rationale: The session was not actually ended when the test proceeded, so the next step sees a signed-in browser where it expects a signed-out one.

pw-n47.rationale: State left by one test (browser zoom) breaks the next test of the same worker and each of the failing tests passes in isolation.

pw-n48.rationale: The failure depends on the browser's viewport behaviour during a capture (a headless-Chromium environment effect on a viewport media query), not on the application logic.

pw-n49.rationale: Two responses for the same endpoint can arrive in either order; the waiter assumes the wrong one is first.

pw-n50.rationale: A fixed wall-clock sleep decides how much work happens; on a slow host the sample is too small, a classic timing flake.

pw-n51.rationale: A second copy of the element exists only until the streamed segment is swapped in; the query lands inside that window.

pw-n52.rationale: A fixed wait decides whether the camera has settled before the click; slow runners need longer, which is timing.

pw-n53.rationale: The test cuts the network and acts before the form's asynchronous load and remount have finished; the order of load and action decides the result.

cy-n18.rationale: Two page-load requests are left unawaited; the order of their responses and the test steps decides the outcome, so it is an async order assumption (and an incompletely stubbed API).

pw-n54.rationale: The test acts on the table before the state it needs (a rendered row) exists; the missing step is the wait for that state.

pw-n55.rationale: An attribute selector that matches both a wrapper and the button is a strict mode violation from the start; the page did not change.

pw-n56.rationale: A substring label locator that is ambiguous within the dialog; nothing about the dialog changed.

pw-n57.rationale: Workspace state left by earlier tests on a shared server breaks later tests; the first test passes alone.
